thread:
Alice Chen: quick FYI — the serializer-sampling canary for bridge-3b-ptq is spiking parse failures (~10.2%). sample size 600. noticed a weird pattern: trailing commas and stray escape sequences in funcall payloads :eyes:
Ben Ortiz: ugh. is this only ptq or also fp32 baseline?
Alice Chen: we ran a small fp32 run (same prompts) — fp32 parse_fail_rate ~0.3%. so regression looks quant-specific.
Carla Nguyen: can you paste a raw failing snippet? might be tokenization->escape interplay.
Alice Chen: paste below (raw stream):
```
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"id":"user:123"},}
```
note trailing comma after object. another class: unclosed string due to backslash before quote: `{"note":"C:\Users\"}` -> model emits single backslash and breaks JSON.
Jamal Price: interesting. could be tokenizer emitting a backslash as a separate token when quantized kernels change byte-level emission. any correlation with sequence length or kvcache enablement?
Alice Chen: yes — higher prefix lengths (kvcache hits) have higher failure rate. suggests kvprefix concatenation boundary is noisy under ptq.
Ben Ortiz: do we have replay ids? can we repro deterministically with the same seed and max_tokens?
Alice Chen: saved a minimal repro in S3: s3://redwood-canaries/serializer-sampling/repro-5322.jsonl — each line has prompt, seed, model config.
Carla Nguyen: for immediate mitigation: canary change proposal — fold in lightweight postproc that runs a minimal sanitize heuristic before parse (wrap in array if single-object trailing commas, escape-fix backslashes). add to canary only (not prod) so we can measure rescue rate.
Jamal Price: also add an A/B branch that disables kv-prefix caching for same model and compare. might help isolate runtime vs model quantization.
Ben Ortiz: what about retry policy? if we re-request with lower temperature or incremental decode, does rate drop?
Alice Chen: tried single soft-retry (same prompt, temp=0.0) — recovered ~25% of failures. Combine with sanitize + retry gives ~80% recovery for canary samples.
Carla Nguyen: propose next steps: 1) run 2x canary cohorts (ptq: kvcache ON vs OFF), 2) attach strict JSON schema checker and record rescue path (retry vs sanitize), 3) run an fp32 control.
Alice Chen: I sketched canary config snippet — adding here for review:
```
canary_config:
  name: serializer-sampling-5322
  model: bridge-3b-ptq
  cohorts:
    - name: kvcache-on
      kvcache: true
    - name: kvcache-off
      kvcache: false
  samples: 1200
  strict_schema: true
  rescue_pipeline: ["wrap_array","repair_trailing_comma","retry_temp0"]
  metrics: ["parse_fail_rate","recovery_by_step","latency_p95"]
```
Ben Ortiz: looks good. add a field for seed reproducibility and record kernels used.
Alice Chen: will add seed + kernel tags. also instrument token-level diffs to catch where the backslash appears.
Jamal Price: timeline?
Alice Chen: launching cohort runs this afternoon. ETA initial results 24h. Ill post the run summary.
deploy-bot: canary run started: serializer-sampling-5322 | bridge-3b-ptq | cohorts: kvcache-on/off | samples=1200
Ben Ortiz: perfect. if we confirm kvcache interaction, we should gate ptq onboard rollouts until we have a mitigation.
Carla Nguyen: agree. also add a unit test in our funcall harness that injects boundary tokens to catch regressions early.
Alice Chen: noted. thanks all — will dump results and curated examples into the ticket once done :thumbsup:
